stem: A Lunesta prescription is four months old and has four prior refills, with one additional refill authorized. What is the most defensible conclusion?

choices.text: Decline because four prior refills exhaust the federal limit.
Dispense indefinitely until the prescriber cancels it.
Require a new prescription because every controlled-drug fill is nonrefillable.
Allow two more refills because the six-month window has two months left.
One additional refill remains within both the five-refill cap and six-month deadline.

explanation.core_reasoning: One additional refill remains within both the five-refill cap and six-month deadline. By contrast, 'Decline because four prior refills exhaust the federal limit.' uses a legal trigger absent from the stem.

related_facts: eszopiclone (Lunesta) is used for treatment of insomnia; it is federal Schedule IV and Massachusetts Schedule IV.
A Schedule III or IV prescription may not be filled or refilled more than six months after issue and may not be refilled more than five times unless renewed by the practitioner.
